Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Conversation responses stalling in us-west-2 (multiple users)

Hi Rishi —

We started seeing user-facing stalls in our conversation UI around 13:58 PDT. The model will stream a few tokens and then pause for 4–12s before resuming; in some sessions it never resumes and the client shows a spinner until the socket times out. Affects ~3% of production traffic for us (US-WEST-2).

Quick details:
- Customer region: us-west-2
- SDK: web 2.1.4 using websocket streaming with chunk_size=1024
- First observed: ~13:58 PDT, March 19
- Impact: stalled responses and some user timeouts

We captured a short profiler trace and client timeline (attached). Can you confirm whether Redwood is seeing elevated tail latencies or dropped streaming frames? This is affecting our paid users; we may need an ETA and temporary mitigations.

Thanks,
Sarah

Quick triage notes (observed 14:10–14:20 PDT):
- We see a spike in tail latency for the streaming websocket path on edge-shard-15 (us-west-2). P50/P95 for non-stream was normal.
- KV cache eviction rate increased ~3x after a daemon restarted on that shard at 12:58 PDT; evictions correlate with higher disk-backed KV lookups and extra backpressure in the token pipeline.
- No model rollout in the last 24h, but there was a kernel patch deployed to the shard host pool at 12:55 PDT (rolled back on a single host at 13:30).

Immediate mitigation applied (14:18 PDT):
- Rebalanced traffic off edge-shard-15 to edge-shard-02 and edge-shard-07 for streaming endpoints.
- Temporarily increased in-memory KV quota for the affected pool (experimental) to reduce lookups.
- Pushed a configuration that short-circuits non-essential prefix caching for streaming path to reduce KV pressure.

Effect: error rate and streaming tail latencies dropped to baseline within ~3m for routed sessions. We are continuing to monitor.

Next actions:
- Marcus: collect kernel patch logs and crosscheck which hosts picked up the 12:55 update; isolate any host with anomalous IO patterns.
- Monica: prepare a customer-safe mitigation note with suggested client SDK adjustments (backoff/retry, reduce chunk_size to 512) and a temporary config we can set on the tenant to avoid timeouts.
- Ben: draft an incident update we can send to the customer; include what we changed and next steps.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Site Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah —
Thanks for the trace and the heads up. Our ops team identified elevated tail latency on a specific edge shard in us-west-2 and applied targeted mitigations at 14:18 PDT (rebalanced traffic + lift KV pressure). We’re seeing normal streaming behavior for new sessions routed to healthy shards.

Suggested immediate customer-side mitigations (safe and reversible):
- Reduce streaming chunk_size to 512 for 24 hours (helps avoid large in-flight frames that amplify backpressure).
- Implement a short client-side retry: if no tokens in 2s, retry the request once with jitter (we’ll provide a sample snippet).
- If you can, turn on the heartbeat ping in the SDK 2.1.4 (opt-in flag) so the connection is kept alive while we stabilize.

We created INC-3421 and are continuing to watch metrics. I’ll follow up in ~2 hours with a status update and an internal postmortem when we have the root cause.

Attachment: mitigation_playbook.pdf (short runbook with SDK snippets, tenant-toggle steps)

Subject: Post-incident notes: us-west-2 streaming slowdown (draft)

Team —
Summary (finalizing for customer and internal postmortem):
Root cause: a partial corruption in the in-memory KV index on edge-shard-15 after a host kernel update (12:55 PDT) caused higher-than-expected eviction activity. That cascadingly increased disk-backed lookups and introduced backpressure in the token dispatch pipeline for websocket streaming sessions. Non-stream endpoints used different caching paths and were largely unaffected.

What we did:
- 14:18 PDT: Rebalanced streaming traffic away from edge-shard-15 to healthy shards.
- 14:18–14:22 PDT: Increased in-memory KV quota and applied prefix-cache short-circuit on affected pool.
- 14:32 PDT: Isolated and rolled back the host that showed the kernel anomaly.

Impact: ~3% of customer traffic for NimbleChat in us-west-2 experienced streaming stalls for 8–12 minutes depending on session routing. No persistent data loss.

Mitigations and next steps:
- Short-term (24–72h): push a hotfix that validates KV index consistency on host start, add a safer fallback route for streaming token dispatch, and publish a customer-facing runbook (done).
- Medium-term (2–6 weeks): improve host kernel rollout gating, mandatory preflight for KV indexes, and increase shard pool redundancy for streaming endpoints.
- Communication: send a customer post-incident summary with root cause and remediation plan (I will finalize the draft).

Please review the draft postmortem in the shared drive and add any notes. I attached the current postmortem draft and a snapshot of metrics we used to assess impact.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.docx, metrics_snapshot.png

Rishi
